en.name: RideZap
en.subtitle: Compare the whole trip
en.short_description: Price a ride, a flight and a hotel across providers and see the cheapest total.
en.description:
RideZap prices one trip across every provider that will quote it.

THREE MODES
Rides, flights, and hotels, each with the search form that mode actually needs — pickup and drop-off, origin and destination, check-in and check-out.

ONE ANSWER
RideZap puts the quotes next to each other and marks the cheapest total, including the conditions attached to it. Open a quote for the detail, then book on the provider's own site.

KEEP IT
Save a trip to watch it, and keep a history of what you have searched. Both are on your device, and both have a clear button.

RideZap does not take your booking or your payment — it hands you to the provider. It earns a commission on some of those links.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing RideZap.

RideZap prices one trip across several travel providers and shows which is cheapest once fees are counted. No account, no sign-in, no demo credentials and no in-app purchase: it opens straight onto the search form.

The one thing to know first: unless this build was compiled with a gateway endpoint and key (RIDEZAP_API_BASE_URL / RIDEZAP_API_KEY), every price you see is produced locally from a bundled sample dataset - it is not a quote from Uber, Lyft, Bolt, Expedia or Booking.com. That is labelled everywhere rather than buried: a non-dismissible banner reading "SAMPLE DATA - these are not live quotes. Nothing here can be booked at these prices." sits above every screen that prints a price (lib/widgets/data_source_banner.dart), and Settings names the active source. Sample fares are re-diced once a minute, so a figure moving while you watch is expected.

Test instructions:
1. Launch. Three tabs across the top - Rides, Flights, Hotels - each with the form that mode needs. Pick-up, drop-off, origin, destination and city fields are free text; they are not checked against a place database, so any text is accepted.
2. Fill the Rides form and tap "Compare ride prices". Results list one quote per provider with the winner marked "CHEAPEST TOTAL".
3. Tap a quote for its full breakdown - base fare, booking fees, trip surcharges and taxes as separate lines - and where it placed against the others.
4. "Book on <provider>" opens that provider's own public website in the browser or their app, with RideZap's referral tag appended (affId=americangroupllc). It is a link out, disclosed on the same screen. RideZap has no checkout, takes no payment and books nothing itself.
5. Save a result to the Watch list, open the Watch list tab, and tap "Re-compare" to see the price-change chip.
6. The History tab records past searches. Settings covers where prices come from, which providers are compared, how RideZap is paid, and can clear the watch list and the history.

Privacy:
• Data collected: nothing about you. There is no account, no sign-up and no profile. Saved trips, search history and the data-source choice are stored on the device with shared_preferences.
• Network: in the default build, none for pricing - quotes are computed on the device. If a gateway endpoint is configured at build time, the itinerary you typed is sent to that endpoint to be priced. Tapping a booking link hands the URL to the system browser.
• Location: none. The app never requests location; pick-up and drop-off are typed.
• Tracking: none. There is no advertising or analytics SDK; the advertising identifier is not read and no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears. A Firebase Crashlytics bootstrap is present but inactive - no Firebase configuration file is included.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
